The forward pass in a large language model (LLM) is the process through which the model predicts the next token in a sequence during inference. The input tokens are first converted into a fixed-length vector representation using the embedding layer. This is done by looking up the corresponding word embeddings in a pre-trained embedding matrix. The embedding matrix, typically denoted as \( \mathbf{E} \), has dimensions \( N \times d \), where \( N \) is the number of tokens in the vocabulary and \( d \) is the embedding dimension (usually in the thousands).
